name: Ritz Carlton Montreal
positioning: The Ritz-Carlton, Montréal: a historic Ritz-Carlton hotel on Sherbrooke Street in the Golden Square Mile, which opened in 1912
best_for: Travelers who want a historic downtown base with museums, shopping and McGill University within a few blocks
Guests who enjoy afternoon tea and French dining

facts.text: Afternoon tea has been a tradition in the Palm Court since 1912.
At Maison Boulud, French cuisine is reinterpreted with local products.
The Palm Court lobby has a Dom Pérignon Champagne Bar serving cocktails and afternoon tea.
Spa St. James has waterfalls and fireplaces.
Suites include fireplaces and separate living spaces.
Bathrooms have marble, heated floors and rainforest shower heads.
The hotel is in the center of the Golden Square Mile, with museums, luxury shopping, nightlife and McGill University within a few blocks.

highlights.text: The hotel opened on New Year's Eve 1912 as the first Ritz-Carlton in North America.
The hotel is the birthplace of Ritz-Carlton Afternoon Tea.
Maison Boulud has a terrace overlooking Sherbrooke Street and a year-round greenhouse with a view of the open kitchen.
The hotel offers a Glatt Kosher Afternoon Tea made in a kitchen certified Kosher Mehadrin.
The Cosner Art Gallery at the hotel presents Canadian painters to guests.

considerations.text: The certified Kosher kitchen is closed on Fridays, and the Glatt Kosher Afternoon Tea requires reservations at least 48 hours in advance.
Spa St. James is by appointment only.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the high-end positioning.
